messages:
Priya: Heads-up — we need to lock sequencing for the Q2 inference runtime changes and product priorities. Two customer asks (cost-sensitive batching and deterministic fallbacks) + internal perf work. Need alignment on infra/dev resources, security review window, and launch gates. Who's free for a quick triage?
Alex G.: I can carve out eng-rt time but we have two hired contractors starting mid-Q2. main constraint is infra bandwidth for dedicated pool changes.
Jin: From runtime side, batching + prefix cache changes are doable in a single sprint if we don't require KV schema changes. Perf reg tests will take ~3 days to run across seq-length buckets.
Marco: Infra: dedicated pool resize + staging clusters need 48h lead time for capacity reservation and rollout. If you want a canary in prod, we need booking by end of week.
Nicole: Security: we'll need a short threat-model + SCA for any new packages. If there are changes that touch token handling or cache persistence, plan for a 1-week review (including fixes). Please surface any third-party libs.
Sam: Proposed plan: we split into two launches — 1) perf & batching (non-persistent cache) and 2) deterministic fallback + cache persistence (if customer requires). That reduces blast radius for security. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
Alex G.: Agree. Sequence 1 then 2. Also recommend a cut of scope: batch tuning + automatic prefix eviction first. Defer persistent KV until infra and sec green.
Jin: +1. For rollout, suggest canary percentages and automated fallback to smaller model if latency regresses. Example rollout plan:
```
canary: 5% for 24h -> 25% for 24h -> 100% if no regression
fallback policy: on p50 latency > 300ms for 10m -> route to smaller-quantized model
metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, error-rate, cost-per-token
```
Marco: That plan is fine. We'll need a downtime window for infra DB schema migration if we do persistent cache. If we avoid persistence initially, no downtime. Also note: autoscaler bump requires ops runbook update.
Nicole: Confirmed: if no persistence and no new KMS integration, security review is a 3-day fast-track. Otherwise 7-10 days. Please annotate in the PR which path we take.
Priya: Customers A and B have asked for deterministic fallback within Q2. If we split launches, how do we communicate timelines to them?
Sam: I'll draft a customer note: "perf/batching beta mid-Q2; deterministic fallback in a follow-up window (target late-Q2)". Will confirm dates by Fri.
Alex G.: Resourcing ask from eng: need 1 eng (3w) + 0.5 SRE (on-call config) for rollout monitoring. Can we get those committed?
Marco: We can allocate 0.5 SRE during the canary window, full SRE for 48h cutover. Infra lead time still applies for capacity.
Priya: Nicole/Jin/Alex — can you each add a one-line gating criterion we can put in the launch checklist?
Jin: Runtime gate: no p95 regressions > 15% vs baseline and cache hit-rate >= 40% on canary.
Nicole: Security gate: SCA + threat-model signed off and no critical findings.
Alex G.: Eng gate: automated regression tests pass and canary rollback works within 5 minutes.
Sam: I'll add those to the rollout doc and spin up a short 30m alignment after lunch. Tentative owners: Priya (product), Alex G. (eng), Jin (runtime), Marco (infra), Nicole (security), Sam (release comms).
Priya: Thanks — please put the rollout doc in the product drive and link it here. Also add required PR labels: "release/canary" "needs-sec-review".
deploy-bot: New deploy window created: 2026-05-12 22:00 UTC -> 2026-05-13 02:00 UTC (ops booking id: ops-8732).
Alex G.: Noted ops window. I'll update the RFC and assign the eng ticket to Maya (contractor) once she starts.
Jin: I'll prep perf test harness and run the seq-length buckets overnight once infra staging is ready.
Marco: I'll confirm capacity reservation and update runbook by EOD.
Nicole: I'll start threat-model draft, tagging related PRs. If anyone adds new deps, ping me.
Sam: Action items captured. Meeting in 30m — sending invite.
Priya: Great — let's try to keep the persistent cache path as optional until infra+sec sign off. :thumbsup:
Alex G.: Agreed. Thanks everyone.
